subject: Subprocessor roster + onshore fallback check for FinKube pilot
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@finkube.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal - FinKube <legal@finkube.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor roster + onshore fallback check for pilot

Hi Jonas and Kimberly,

Thanks again for the quick demo earlier this week — the FinKube security team wants to confirm a couple of items before we can finalize the pilot contract:

1) Can you share your current subprocessor roster (including temporary/ephemeral agents) and indicate which processors touch cleartext logs?
2) For EU-resident traffic, do you have an onshore fallback plan if a transit partner is unavailable (we need proof of an onshore routing path and estimated RTO)?

Our legal team will review any documented controls but asked for the roster + a short dataflow sketch so they can map responsibilities.

Would appreciate the files by end-of-day Monday (their security review is on Tuesday).

Cheers,
Elena Ortiz
Security Operations Lead
FinKube

Attachment: (none)

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@finkube.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + onshore fallback check for pilot

Elena —

Thanks for the note. Attaching our latest internal roster (subprocessor_roster_v2.csv) and a quick one-page dataflow sketch (dataflow_sketch.pdf). High level:

- We have a small set of persistent subprocessors (metrics, observability, KMS) and a handful of ephemeral edge relays for burst traffic.
- Ephemeral relays do not persist user payloads beyond the request lifecycle; they forward encrypted payloads to our runtime.
- For EU traffic, we maintain an onshore fallback runbook that can route to a reserved EU-only pool (documentation attached as eu_onshore_fallback_plan.docx). This plan includes estimated reconfiguration RTO (30–90 minutes depending on session stickiness) and a list of providers we can promote to onshore mode.

Notes and open items:
- We flagged one temporary analytics bridge (EdgeSight-lite) in the roster — marked in the CSV as "temp" and requires SOC2 evidence if FinKube wants long-term access.
- Naomi, can you confirm the KMS/HSM vendor (KeyGate) encryption in transit/at-rest attestation and whether we have export-control constraints?

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute walk-through tomorrow to step through the roster and the fallback playbook.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_v2.csv, dataflow_sketch.pdf, eu_onshore_fallback_plan.docx

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@finkube.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Legal - FinKube <legal@finkube.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + onshore fallback check for pilot

Elena —

Quick follow-up from our security/compliance side after internal review of the attached roster and fallback doc:

- KeyGate (KMS/HSM) is validated for EU residency and has a signed attestation on file. Naomi, confirm the latest attestation link?
- The temporary analytics bridge (EdgeSight-lite) is used for aggregated telemetry only; we do not send PII. We can remove that processor from the pilot scope if FinKube requires.
- For the onshore fallback, we can pre-provision the reserved EU pool under the dedicated capacity contract (this will require a brief procurement amendment — I put an estimated delta below).

Procurement delta estimate for reserved EU pool:
- Monthly reserved capacity uplift: ~$9K
- Expected cutover time: 45–90 minutes

Next steps we propose:
1) Naomi to attach KeyGate attestation and a short SOC2 excerpt.
2) We remove EdgeSight-lite from the pilot scope (if FinKube prefers) and resend an amended roster.
3) If FinKube signs off on the fallback uplift, we will issue an amendment (DocuSign link to follow).

Elena — are you OK with the above approach? If so, I'll draft the amendment and route to procurement/legal.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: (will attach KeyGate_attestation.pdf after Naomi confirms)

From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@finkube.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Legal - FinKube <legal@finkube.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + onshore fallback check for pilot

Thanks, Kimberly/Jonas — this is helpful.

We have two quick asks before we can clear the security gating:
1) Please remove EdgeSight-lite from the pilot roster (or mark it as not-in-scope) and resend the CSV.
2) We need the KeyGate attestation and a SOC2 excerpt uploaded to our secure reviewer portal. Once those are available, Legal will confirm the fallback amendment and I will request procurement to sign the DocuSign amendment.

We plan to complete the security review by end-of-day Wednesday once the above is uploaded. If you're short on time, the DocuSign amendment link is OK to receive tomorrow and we'll pause signature until evidence is posted.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — happy to take the 30-minute walk-through if helpful.

Best,
Elena Ortiz
Security Operations Lead
FinKube
